items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: You couldn't even tell you it was Andrew Kimball. One of the greatest reading trumpet and jazz trumpets. He was Andrew Kimball, Joe Oliver, and Mario Perez. That was the stiffest trumpet players they had around here.

ctx.x: Beverly Garden. That's Beverly Garden. So we had mean old man, Kimball and all of us. Papa Celestine, he went with Rizzley too. And we left Hampton Benson, I originally being a trauma player at South. And T.O., he quit P-Rone, he went on over there with us too. So we stuck out there and- You played drums then? He stuck out there a long time, making good money. So well, the boys got to say they want to go back to the red light. Went on back to the red light and played at King Holler. King Holler was at Pete…

items.title: Bill Matthews Interview, 1959-03-10
items.q: So, finally, I stuck there with Zooty and old man Kimmel... I said, well I got a job for you if you want it... I went back to St. Louis to the jazz

ctx.x: And a wonderful band. Nice musical band. So, Nora said, old man, I mean, young man, I said, yes, sir. He's calling me, I said, I'm sickly, you know. So, you come to my house, you can stay there, you eat and sleep, do anything you want. I said, I got a place, I'm going to stay at your house. I said, no, I don't want you to stay there. I got a place, by it. It's me and my wife. I don't want you to stay there. I said, before we could get things straight, now, here comes Zooty. So, the singer, he comes through, he…
Not to talk. And he was playing
